_note: A reading of the whole public forum (1,464 topics, all categories, 2020 to 2026), done 2026-11-27. Quotes are verbatim and carry the thread they come from. Interpretive lines are labelled. Network counts come from matching partner names in the full text of partners' own posts; reply counts are not used.

staff.intro: The Foundation's team wrote most in 2020-2023. What they said then still reads as the house view; after 2023 staff posts nearly stop.

fund.q: we fund irrespective of size and age of the org - the only bias is around the ambition and audaciousness of the approach, the willingness and ability to introspect, learn, pivot and partner, and chase end goals more than supply side metrics
Small, untied grants of 3 to 12 lakh a year for 3 years, for rewilding, ecosystem restoration and localized production
happy to incubate/fund ideas that are non-extractive and regenerative, scale as an idea, and create livelihoods for many
beneficiary headcounts are a hangover from the savior complex era; watch biodiversity, footprints and livelihood resilience instead
We would love to talk and offer whatever support we can
fund.who: Nithin Kamath, on private models that pay farmers to green land

fund.q: Please do NOT use this for proposals and pitches ... send anything long term (3-5 years) with a plan to info@rainmatter.org

thesis.q: Can we move from the current instinct and default of 'intervening' which pre-supposes much, to 'responding' ... we cannot afford small, even if great, pockets of change
the net sum of all the declared successes should have translated to a very different landscape
thesis.who: Sameer Shisodia, asking for failure stories

thesis.q: It's primarily a consumption problem. The data says that.
part of the solution seems to be to make it more expensive, not less, to buy air-conditioning, and cross subsidize the other, scalable and smarter solutions. Change my mind
we're struggling with a clear thesis in terms of imagining what needles might be moved
thesis.who: Sameer Shisodia, on the urban climate problem

thesis.q: air quality needs follow up action, not more research; airsheds as the unit for coordinated action
fund outcome-linked FPO evidence, not more description; the enterprise layer is the common gap across FPCs, SHGs and forest communities

open.q: Offered the Foundation office to host a cross-organisation leadership discussion 'without our org hats'
Inbound funding paused in favour of a thesis and announced 'chases'; no chase has been posted in that thread since
A pledge to help the first 5 organisations list on the Social Stock Exchange; by 2026 still early days

network.intro: From the full text of partners' own posts (who names whom; not replies): 180 partner pairs. The `with` lists in work items add 55 state-tagged pairs.
ties: name each other 11 times; Gram Swabhimaan runs through Gram Vikas villages
6 mentions; same corporations in Mumbai and Uttar Pradesh
6; film screenings in Gram Vikas villages
6; climate-risk planning inside Assam's urban programme
network.inwardNote: Named by the most peers. Several have few or no work items on this page (IIHS, CEEW, MSSRF), so a blank here does not mean absent from the ecosystem.
network.isolatedNote: Post a lot, name no other partner. Introductions would add most here.

themes.intro: 374 work items re-grouped into shared themes (an item can carry several). The three widest are not natural assets at all.
rows: Farmers for Forests, Gurukula, Shola Trust, NCF, ERA
WCS, NCF, A Rocha, Wild Shaale
notes: Heat and bamboo look widespread but are mostly one actor each (Asar 9 of 16 heat items; Industree 10 of 11 bamboo).
Human-wildlife conflict has 10 actors and three species across 11 states; no state page connects them.
Nilgiris and Western Ghats restoration is one cluster split across three state pages: Gurukula, Shola Trust, NCF, Keystone, Forest Way, Upstream, ERA.

ring.intro: A second ring of organisations that several partners work through. None is on the partner list; a newcomer to these places would want these names first.
ring.alliances: Existing tables partners already sit at: Sense of the House alliance, Alliance to Push Harder, ClimateRISE, Vikalp Sangam, ERA-India, URC-IS, NFSSM Alliance, SHIFT Transport Coalition, Network for Water Secure Gram Panchayats, GROW+ landscapes, Tech4Good Climate Coalition, Bengaluru Heat Collective (11 members).

funders.intro: Co-funding is the easiest introduction. Shared funders named in partners' own posts:
rows: 6: Gurukula, Sahjeevan, SlamOutLoud, Technology for Wildlife, Veditum, WCS
EdelGive, Tata entities, UNDP, UNEP, SVP
funders.money: 77 rupee amounts sit next to grant, fund or CSR words in partner posts (for example Biome: Rs 1.28 crore CSR plus Rs 69.3 lakh farmer co-financing in Kolar; Waste Warriors: Rs 8.5 lakh Resilience Fund award; Janaagraha: Rainmatter partnership renewed for 4 years from April 2025).

health: The forum itself has shifted from conversation (2023: half of all posts and views) to noticeboard (2026: most new threads are single posts; average views per new thread fell roughly tenfold). Staff posting nearly stopped after 2023. This page exists partly because of that shift.
